body:
Near death, grace come — by himself or a kinsman's mouth: the instant ascent-rite. Lay the whole course in the pupil and cleanse it; set Time-night, marrow-cutter; cut the marrow-bonds joint by joint; seat his awareness at Brahmā's hole. Then the joining full-offering as before — till at its end the life goes out Lord-undivided. Enjoyers get a second full-offering (their station, their life melting then; no conduct after). Whisper brahma-knowledge in his ear — grasping-natured, it wakes grasping in the just-waked beast-mind. Samayins too may hear it read. The marked seedless — for dullards and the graced: at Śiva's hand-gift, picture in the right palm a southeast triangle, flame-grim, phaṭ-sparking, ringed with outer wind-wheels; drop in a seed; burn his birth-power with phaṭ upon phaṭ kindled up and down; clap that hand on his crown. Seedless for both — wrecking the power to make its own work. Even the unmoving may be raised: picture the trembling pupil hung in wind's city, grown light — light on the scales to see.

The passage moves in two parts. First, sadyaḥ: near-death with descent-arisen → whole course placed/purified → Kālarātrī marrow-cutter placed → marrow-bonds split → Brahma-hole consciousness made → joining full-offering → life gone forth Lord-undivided; enjoyer-wisher gets second full-offering (life-dissolution; no remaining conduct); brahmavidyā in ear (grasping-natured, wakes grasping in awakened-beast-consciousness); samayins too entitled. Second, nirbījā: marked seedless for fool/descent-come → Śiva-hand-gift rite (triangle southeast flame-terrible phaṭ-spark outer-wind-wheel maṇḍala in right hand, seed cast, up-down-phaṭ series burning birth-power, hand thrown on crown) = seedless for both, own-work-power-destroying; immovables initiable (wind-city-abiding, trembling, light-made, balance-light).
terms: sadyaḥ (instant), samutkramaṇa (ascent), kālarātrī (Time-night), marmakartanī (marrow-cutter), brahmarandhra (Brahma-hole), nirbījā (seedless), Śiva-hasta (Śiva-hand).
function: Two rites for urgency and incapacity: instant ascent (sadyaḥ) and seedless initiation (nirbījā).
local_context: A14 (putraka) precedes; A15 teaches urgent/seedless rites; A16 (parokṣa) follows.
